items.title: CNF Graduates Cohort 3 of Skill Scale-Up Programme, Charges Young Nigerians to Lead With Purpose
items.imageAlt: CNF Skill Scale-Up Cohort 3 graduates and staff at the graduation ceremony in Kurudu, Abuja
items.excerpt: CNF celebrated the graduation of Cohort 3 of the Skill Scale-Up Programme at its Kurudu hub, with Founder Chiggy Nsofor urging graduates to lead with purpose and pay it forward.
items.body:
The Chiggy Nsofor Foundation (CNF) on 22nd of May 2026, marked another significant milestone in its mission to empower Nigerian youth, as it officially graduated the third cohort of the Skill Scale-Up Programme (SSU) at the CNF Skill Scale-Up Hub in Kurudu, Abuja.

The ceremony was a celebration not just of skills acquired, but of resilience, growth, and the quiet but powerful transformation that happens when young people are given the right environment and the right support.

The Graduating "STARS"- as students of the programme are fondly called, took turns expressing what the journey meant to them, with many describing the programme as a life-changing experience and voicing their wish that it could continue indefinitely. Their words spoke to something deeper than technical training; they spoke of confidence found, of futures reimagined.

One of the most moving moments of the day came from Abbas, an alumnus of CNF's inaugural Cohort 1, who returned to share his story with the newest set of graduates. Abbas, who is now carving out a career in photography and videography, stood as a living testimony to what the CNF experience can produce, not just a certificate, but a trajectory.

In her keynote address, CNF Founder Chiggy Nsofor delivered a message that was both celebratory and deeply personal. She acknowledged the graduating STARS for their commitment throughout the programme, noting that showing up consistently, even when the journey was tough, was itself an act of courage.

"Nothing you experience in this program happened by me alone," she said. "It happens because of the team called the CNF Army." The tribute drew warm applause for the CNF staff whose dedication makes every cohort possible.

With the warmth of someone who had watched them grow during the course of the program, Chiggy left the graduates with a charge they could carry for life: "I do not have to convince you that you are capable of impact, because you have already done it." She challenged the graduates to take that same energy beyond the walls of the programme, to pay it forward. To give advice when someone needs it, to mentor others coming behind them, and to be living proof that CNF's investment in them was well placed.

"Love is the reason this foundation exists," she told the gathering. "Go out and spread that love, in your workplace, in your family, in your community."

Our Founder extended her gratitude to CNF's partners, supporters, and the families of the graduates, recognising that the learning journey of every STAR is supported by a wider circle of people who believe in the vision.

As Cohort 3 steps into the next chapter, they carry with them not just the skills developed over the course of the programme, but the values, the mindset, and the community that CNF has built around them.

The Chiggy Nsofor Foundation continues to stay true to its commitment in building futures and transforming lives.

Read the full media coverage of the graduation:
The Reporters (https://thereporters.com.ng/2026/05/23/fg-urged-to-partner-ngos-on-youth-empowerment-skill-acquisition/) and The News Guru (https://thenewsguru.ng/news/skills-acquisition-antidote-to-crime-ngo-tells-fg/).

items.title: Beyond Handwashing: CNF Brings Comprehensive Hygiene Education to Dutse, Bwari
items.imageAlt: CNF hygiene education outreach session with students at Total Child Model School, Dutse, Bwari
items.excerpt: CNF delivered a comprehensive personal hygiene curriculum to students at Total Child Model School, Dutse, Bwari, covering seven key areas from hand hygiene to menstrual health.
items.body:
On May 8, 2026, the Chiggy Nsofor Foundation team stepped into the classrooms of Total Child Model School, Dutse, Bwari, Abuja, with one clear mission: to equip young students with the knowledge and awareness they need to take care of their bodies and their communities. What unfolded was an interactive, student-centred session that covered far more than handwashing alone.

The outreach delivered a comprehensive personal hygiene curriculum, recognising that good health begins with the habits practiced every single day. Across the session, students were introduced to seven key hygiene areas: Hand Hygiene, Hair Hygiene, Oral Hygiene, Menstrual Hygiene, Clothing Hygiene, Body Hygiene, and Skincare Hygiene.

Each topic was addressed with practical tips students could act on immediately, not just within school walls, but at home and in their communities. The session also paid particular attention to menstrual hygiene, an often-overlooked yet critical area of health education for young girls.

The CNF team engaged students through conversation, demonstrations, and open discussion, creating an atmosphere where young people felt comfortable asking questions and sharing experiences. The approach reflected CNF's broader belief that education works best when it meets people where they are. When young people understand how to care for their bodies, they show up differently- in class, at home, and in their communities. That is the foundation of everything we do.

The outreach also reinforced the significance of World Hand Hygiene Day as a global reminder that simple hygiene practices remain one of the most powerful tools for preventing disease. For many of the students at Total Child Model School, the session offered not just new information, but a renewed sense of confidence in taking charge of their own wellbeing.

The Chiggy Nsofor Foundation remains committed to showing up in classrooms, communities, and conversations, wherever there is a need and an opportunity to transform lives.

items.title: CNF Commemorates International Women's Day at AGGS Gudu, Abuja
items.imageAlt: CNF education outreach session with students at AGGS Gudu, Abuja
items.excerpt: CNF marked International Women's Day at AGGS Gudu with sessions on self-belief, goal-setting, and resilience under the theme "Give to Gain."
items.body:
In commemoration of International Women's Day 2026, Chiggy Nsofor Foundation held an impactful outreach at Anglican Girls Grammar School (AGGS) under the theme "Give to Gain." The highlight of the event was a powerful session led by our Founder, Chiggy Nsofor, who focused on the very foundation of success: self-belief.

In a moving display of affirmation, Chiggy led the students in a collective affirmation, urging them to internalize the message: "I am a girl, my dreams are valid, I believe in myself, and I will change the world."

The event was defined by heartfelt conversations rather than a standard lecture. Chiggy addressed the students on "The power of a girl who dreams and believes in herself," tackling the internal barriers that often prevent young women from pursuing ambitious paths.

Chiggy provided the students with a roadmap for success, centering the discussion on three critical pillars: reinforcing that a girl's potential is fueled by her unwavering belief in her own future; teaching that intentional goal-setting is the bridge between a dream and its realization; and reminding every student that success is found in the courage to believe in oneself even when circumstances become challenging.

In a poignant moment of reflection, Chiggy challenged the students to look ahead. She told them to imagine who they will be in 40 years' time and asked if they would be proud of the woman they had become. She reminded them that the woman they will be in the future is built on the choices they make today, emphasizing that now is the time to build the character and skills to become that woman.

During the interactive session, students courageously shared their dreams and the specific fears, social, financial, and personal, that they face. The CNF team provided practical advice, reinforcing the idea that a student's potential is defined not by her current circumstances, but by her courage to dream.

In a post-event meeting, the Principal of AGGS, Mrs. Nkiru Nwofor, extended her deep appreciation to the team. She noted that the school is eager to host more initiatives that challenge the students to unlock their full potential.

"We are more than glad to partner with CNF to improve in the aspects of skill acquisition and financial literacy," Mrs. Nwofor stated. "It is essential to get them ready for the future so they can be financially independent at a very young age."

The outreach concluded with a strong sense of momentum. By providing encouragement and sharing lived experiences, the CNF team left with a reinforced belief in the brilliance of the AGGS students. These young women are proving to be the change-makers of today, ready to lead with sharp minds and open hearts.

CNF remains committed to this partnership, looking forward to future collaborations that arm these students with the practical skills needed to thrive in a modern economy.

items.title: A New Chapter of Impact: Skill Scale-Up Cohort 3 Tech Batch Begins
items.imageAlt: Skill Scale-Up Cohort 3 tech orientation session at the CNF training hub
items.excerpt: CNF opens its third cohort of the Skill Scale-Up Programme, welcoming a new generation of digital and tech trainees.
items.body:
Today marked the beginning of a transformative journey for Skill Scale-Up Cohort 3. This specialized tech batch represents our latest commitment to bridging the gap and empowering the next generation of innovators.

During our orientation, we set the bar high. In the rapidly evolving tech landscape, we emphasized that dedication and continuous growth are no longer just advantages, and they are non-negotiable requirements for success.

Our founder, Chiggy Nsofor, during her address to cohort 3, urged every STAR to bring their "A-Game". She reminded the STARS that while CNF provides the platform, their individual excellence is what will truly open doors in the industry.

The charge given by our founder to our STARS is that "as they learn from the program, they must also lift those around them by teaching others". This ensures that the technical knowledge gained in this cohort doesn't stop with the individual but flows back into the community, creating a ripple effect of impact.

At Chiggy Nsofor Foundation, we are building more than just technical experts; we are cultivating the next generation of mentors. As our STARS immerse themselves in high-demand tech skills, we have challenged them to extend the circle of kindness.

We are incredibly excited to witness this cohort transform their raw potential into the kind of leadership that reshapes industries and strengthens local communities.

This isn't just a training program; it is the start of a legacy.

items.title: Celebrating the Graduation of CNF's Second Skill Scale-Up Cohort
items.imageAlt: CNF Skill Scale-Up Cohort 2 graduates and staff at the graduation ceremony
items.excerpt: CNF celebrates the graduation of Cohort 2 of the Skill Scale-Up Programme, 19 dedicated STARS who completed an intensive three-month training cycle.
items.body:
November marks another significant milestone for Chiggy Nsofor Foundation as we celebrate the successful graduation of the second cohort of our Skill Scale-Up Program.

Over the past 3 months, 19 dedicated STARS engaged in an intensive training cycle that combined skill advancement with personal growth, discipline, and character building. Throughout the program, they showed remarkable dedication and consistency, successfully completing their coursework, practical sessions, and capstone projects, a true reflection of their commitment to excellence.

Cohort 2 carried forward the momentum of the first cohort, embracing a fast-paced learning model rooted in accountability, collaboration, and hands-on application. During the course of the training, they demonstrated steady progress, growing in confidence, expanding their digital creativity, and working together effectively to turn ideas into real outcomes. This graduation reflects a deeper alignment to the standards expected in today's tech-based and digital-driven industries.

One of the most memorable parts of the ceremony was the retrospective presentation, "Cohort 1: The Story So Far." The presentation highlighted their journey beyond graduation, spotlighting how their skills have evolved into taking initiative and creating impact in their personal lives and communities. Their story served as a compelling reminder of the long-term value of intentional skill building, mentorship, and character formation.

A highlight of the ceremony was the speech by our Founder, Chiggy Nsofor. She passionately reinforced the idea that character is the foundation of lasting success, noting that while skills open doors, character keeps them open. Her message focused on four core pillars: never stop learning; serve even when there is little or no payment; be a person of impact; and love, the reason the Skill Scale-Up program exists.

Bringing her address to a close, she shared heartfelt gratitude, recognizing the dedication, selflessness, and unwavering support of the phenomenal CNF Army.

The ceremony was particularly touching as parents and guardians expressed deep appreciation to CNF for the invaluable work being done, sharing moving testimonies about how the lives of their children and wards have already started changing positively since joining the program.

As we celebrate this milestone, we are reminded once again why this program matters: young people have immense potential, and when they are supported intentionally and given the right structure, they thrive. CNF continues to champion their development, preparing them to step into the world as capable, self-assured, and purpose-driven youths who will influence the tech, digital, creative and economic space positively.

We look forward to witnessing the continued expansion of their impact and growth. Congratulations to the Cohort 2 STARS.

Read more about this milestone in the media: TimesReporters (https://timesreporters.com/chiggy-nsofor-foundation-celebrates-cohort-2-graduation-of-skill-scale-up-project/) and Independent Newspaper (https://independent.ng/foundation-celebrates-cohort-two-graduation-of-skill-scale-up-in-web-development-photography-others/).

items.title: CNF Enhances Healthcare Access with Drug Donations in Jikwoyi, Abuja
items.imageAlt: CNF team and Jikwoyi Primary Health Care staff at a drug donation outreach
items.excerpt: CNF donated essential medications to Jikwoyi Primary Health Care Clinic, strengthening affordable healthcare access for vulnerable families.
items.body:
Our commitment to our mission to provide essential support to vulnerable communities was demonstrated via our medical donation outreach at Jikwoyi Primary Health Care Clinic.

The core of the outreach centered on the donation of a substantial inventory of medications. Recognizing the high financial barrier many vulnerable families face in accessing basic treatment, we strategically included a diverse range of high-demand drugs.

The donated supplies included antimalarials crucial for tackling the endemic threat of malaria; broad-spectrum antibiotics for treating common bacterial infections; analgesics and anti-inflammatories to manage pain, fever, and discomfort; and IV fluids and infusions vital for stabilizing severely dehydrated or critically ill patients.

Crucially, we stipulated that these high-quality medicines will be sold to the community at a significantly subsidized price. This sustainable model ensures the facility can maintain a revolving fund to restock supplies while making life-saving healthcare affordable for every resident.

This initiative is a tangible expression of Chiggy Nsofor Foundation's broader healthcare mission, which is dedicated to breaking down financial barriers to medical services for vulnerable individuals and communities across Nigeria. By focusing on primary health care centers, CNF aims to strengthen the grassroots institutions that are the first line of defense against disease.

Pharm. Yakubu Awodi, a representative from the Abuja Municipal Area Council, was in attendance and offered high praise for the Foundation's philanthropic efforts. In his remarks, he commended CNF for taking proactive steps to support public health and stressed the vital need for sustainability and accountability within such programs. An agreement was reached that the drugs will be sold with a 1.08 markup from the initial cost price.

Nr. Sally Adegbite, the Matron of Jikwoyi Primary Healthcare Clinic, expressed her profound gratitude. She highlighted that the donation was not just about drugs but about restoring faith in the clinic's ability to serve the community effectively. The supplies are expected to drastically improve their capacity to treat a higher volume of patients with dignity and efficiency.

Chiggy Nsofor Foundation's action in Jikwoyi serves as a powerful reminder of the impact that private philanthropy can have when directly targeted at the point of greatest need, cementing CNF's role as a proactive partner in community development.

items.title: CNF Graduates First Cohort of the Skill Scale-Up Programme
items.imageAlt: First Skill Scale-Up cohort graduates and CNF team at the graduation ceremony
items.excerpt: Twenty-one STARS graduated from CNF's inaugural Skill Scale-Up cohort after four months of intensive training across digital, vocational, and character-building tracks.
items.body:
The atmosphere was filled with pride, joy, and excitement on 11th of July 2025 as Chiggy Nsofor Foundation (CNF) marked a significant milestone with the graduation of the first cohort of the Skill Scale-Up Program. Twenty-one students proudly crossed the threshold from training to opportunity, having completed 4 months of intensive and transformative learning experience across vital skill areas.

The graduating cohort were trained in Web Development, Digital Marketing, Photography and Videography, Catering, Hair Styling, Makeup Artistry, Content Creation, Entrepreneurship, and the Total Man Concept, a holistic curriculum designed to prepare young people not just for jobs, but for purpose-driven lives.

The graduation ceremony, held at Kurudu, Abuja, Nigeria, was a heartwarming celebration of growth, resilience, and the power of community. In attendance were families, supporters, and members of the CNF community, all gathered to celebrate the achievements of the graduates, affectionately called STARS.

In her address, Chiggy Nsofor, the visionary Founder and CEO of CNF, extended her heartfelt appreciation to everyone who contributed to making the day a success. She gave special recognition to the CNF Army, the Foundation's dedicated team, for their tireless efforts and unwavering commitment.

Speaking to the graduates, Chiggy offered both heartfelt congratulations and a charge for the road ahead. "Learning a skill is vital," she said, "but what is even more important is character. Character will sustain you. Remember, if you have a bad attitude, you can never make it. Where talent might get you to the door, character will keep you in the room."

Her words struck a powerful chord, reminding the STARS that technical ability alone isn't enough; integrity, humility, and consistency will be their lifelong allies.

Chiggy encouraged the graduates to carry forward the values instilled in them during the program with three key messages: never stop learning; serve without expectation; and live a life of impact.

As the event concluded, the air was thick with inspiration. These 21 trailblazers are not just leaving with skills; they're leaving with vision, direction, and a strong community behind them.

With programs like Skill Scale-Up, Chiggy Nsofor Foundation continues to lead the charge in equipping young Nigerians with the tools, values, and confidence they need to thrive in today's world and shape tomorrow.

Read more in the media: Leadership Newspaper (https://leadership.ng/foundation-graduates-21-youths-in-skill-empowerment-programme/) and Times Newspaper (https://timesreporters.com/chiggy-nsofor-foundation-empowers-21-youths-through-skill-scale-up-cohort-1/).

items.title: Project WASH: CNF Promotes Hygiene Among Secondary School Students
items.imageAlt: CNF volunteer distributing hygiene kits to students during Project WASH
items.excerpt: CNF executed Project WASH in Fountain International Schools and Eminent Royal Crown Academy, Keffi, reaching over 100 students with hygiene education and supplies.
items.body:
Chiggy Nsofor Foundation took a significant step with the execution of its Project Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) in Fountain International Schools and Eminent Royal Crown Academy, Keffi, Nasarawa State. This initiative aims to instill proper hygiene practices and improve sanitation among students.

The outreach commenced with interactive sessions where the students learned the importance of regular handwashing and proper waste disposal. Demonstrations on effective handwashing techniques were conducted, emphasizing the role of hygiene in preventing diseases.

In addition to teaching the fundamentals of handwashing and disease prevention, CNF introduced a broader hygiene education segment that included oral care, body care, skincare, clothing care, and menstrual hygiene for female students to understand menstruation, using sanitary pads, and safely disposing of menstrual items.

The outreach featured a series of activities including distribution of sanitary materials such as mops, disinfectants, detergents and trash cans. Additionally, hygiene kits containing items such as soap, hand sanitizers, sponge, toothpaste and toothbrush, hair combs, deodorants and other hygiene kits were also distributed to the students.

Over 100 students benefited from Project WASH, which aimed to improve sanitation, educate students on a holistic approach to personal hygiene and self-care.

According to CNF's program officer, Pamela I., "We believe hygiene is comprehensive. When students understand how to care for every aspect of their body and environment, they become agents of change in their homes and communities."

School heads expressed gratitude, highlighting that the initiative had opened meaningful conversations around topics often neglected in formal education. "Our school and students are more than grateful for this initiative," said Mrs Uju Godwin, Head Teacher of Eminent Royal Crown Academy. "It is a rare opportunity that they will not take for granted. With these items given to us, the students are better equipped to take responsibility for their health."

items.title: CNF Launches the Skill Scale-Up Programme to Empower Youths in Digital and Vocational Skills
items.imageAlt: CNF instructor leading a Skill Scale-Up classroom training session
items.excerpt: CNF officially launched the Skill Scale-Up Project at its Kurudu Training Hub, opening a four-month programme for practical, in-demand skills and personal development.
items.body:
The Chiggy Nsofor Foundation (CNF) has officially launched the Skill Scale-Up Project in Kurudu, Abuja, a dynamic initiative designed to equip young people with practical, in-demand skills for success in today's evolving economy.

The SSU Project is a 4-month training program designed to build both practical abilities and personal development. The Skill Scale-Up Project offers a tailored blend of vocational and technical skills empowering youth with career-ready competencies and entrepreneurial insight.

In addition to their coursework, students also have access to recreational activities designed to keep them engaged, relaxed, and active throughout the program.

Located in Kurudu Community, Abuja, CNF Training Hub opened its doors with an inspiring orientation session on Monday, April 7th, 2025. The event welcomed a vibrant group of students all committed to growth, impact and transformation.

In an encouraging message to the students, Chiggy Nsofor, the Founder, spoke about success being collaborative. She challenged them to bring their best efforts to the program: "Bring in your A-game, just as CNF has brought its A-game to you," she said.

During the orientation, students shared their aspirations for joining the program. One of the beneficiaries, ThankGod, a Digital Marketing student, stated that his goal for joining the program is to acquire a skill and make use of the skill to empower himself financially.

Following the successful orientation, classes have officially commenced and students have fully resumed their training. The energy at the hub is vibrant, with participants already immersed in learning.

The Hub is fully equipped with the tools and resources needed for each course, ensuring every student has hands-on access to their craft. The program also boasts some of the best tutors in the field, industry professionals passionate about mentorship and skilled in guiding learners from the basics to mastery.

The project combines expert instruction with real-world application, offering a holistic educational experience. The program is open to youth from all backgrounds, reflecting CNF's commitment to diversity, empowerment, and long-term community impact.

The Skill Scale-Up Project is more than a training program; it's a mission toward empowerment, self-reliance, and real change. With the energy already building in Kurudu, the journey towards impact has officially begun.

items.title: CNF Brightens the Festive Season with Food Relief Outreach in Gonin Gora, Kaduna
items.imageAlt: CNF Festive Food Relief outreach with community members and relief supplies in Gonin Gora
items.excerpt: CNF's Festive Food Relief outreach in Gonin Gora, Kaduna brought essential food items to over 100 families during the holiday season.
items.body:
Chiggy Nsofor Foundation (CNF) has brought smiles to the faces of vulnerable individuals in Gonin Gora community located in Kaduna state through a Humanitarian project tagged "Festive Food Relief (FFR)". The outreach, which was held on the 7th of December, 2024, was an impactful initiative conducted as part of the Foundation's ongoing efforts to support and uplift vulnerable individuals in underserved communities.

CNF's Festive Food Relief Outreach aimed to address the immediate needs of vulnerable persons by providing and distributing essential food items to ensure that several households in Gonin Gora can celebrate the festive season with joy and dignity. Some of the essential food items provided by CNF included garri, rice, palm oil, maggi, salt, and more.

Through this initiative, CNF reinforced her commitment to improving the lives of vulnerable people and community support. The outreach not only provided material relief but also provided a sense of hope and togetherness among the residents of Gonin Gora, Kaduna State.

Both the Community Head, Sarki anguwan Bijeh, and the Counsellor, Hon. Danladi Dogo thanked CNF for their support and prayed for the progress of the Foundation. A beneficiary of our relief efforts in Gonin Gora, Mrs Abigail, like many other beneficiaries also expressed deep appreciation to CNF for the food items she received on behalf of her family.

By addressing the nutritional needs, the Foundation's FFR Outreach has significantly impacted the lives of over 100 families in Gonin Gora, Kaduna State, ensuring that the festive season is a time of celebration and not hardship.

CNF continues to embody the spirit of giving and compassion, making a meaningful difference in the lives of many and helping them to live a better quality of life.

items.title: CNF and FemPower Empower Young Girls in Mpape with Menstrual Hygiene Education
items.imageAlt: CNF and FemPower menstrual hygiene education outreach with students at L.E.A Primary School, Mpape
items.excerpt: CNF and FemPower partnered at L.E.A Primary School, Mpape, delivering menstrual hygiene education, dignity kits, and school supplies to young girls.
items.body:
Chiggy Nsofor Foundation (CNF) and FemPower partnered at L.E.A Primary School, Mpape, on the 11th of October, to host an impactful outreach focused on menstrual hygiene education and girl-child empowerment. The initiative aimed to equip young girls with the knowledge, confidence, and resources they need to stay healthy and focused on their education.

The event brought together key partners, including Wazobia FM, Cool FM, Nigeria Info FM, Air Peace, and FIDA (The International Federation of Women Lawyers), all committed to advancing gender equality and promoting access to menstrual hygiene products.

The program commenced with an interactive session led by Dorkong Rimdan, CEO and Founder of FemPower, who delivered essential education on menstrual hygiene management and self-care practices. Her presentation provided practical guidance designed to break stigmas and encourage open dialogue about menstrual health.

Following the educational segment, Chiggy Nsofor, Founder and CEO of the Chiggy Nsofor Foundation, inspired the students with a message of empowerment. She challenged traditional stereotypes by emphasizing that women and girls can pursue any career path they choose. To reinforce this message of self-belief, she led the students in singing "I Know I Can Be What I Want to Be."

The event also featured a workshop on making reusable sanitary pads, a sustainable alternative that supports both health and environmental goals. In addition, CNF provided material support to the school, donating 16 cartons of soft-care pads and over 15 packs of tissue paper to help address the ongoing need for menstrual hygiene supplies.

This collaboration between CNF and FemPower marks a significant step toward promoting menstrual health awareness and empowering young girls in underserved communities. Through initiatives like this, both organizations continue to champion equal opportunities, ensuring that every girl has the confidence and tools to reach her full potential.

items.title: New Kuchingoro IDP Camp Receives Free Medical Services, Scholarships, and Food Relief
items.imageAlt: CNF Project HEEM outreach with community members at New Kuchingoro IDP camp
items.excerpt: CNF's Project HEEM outreach at New Kuchingoro IDP camp delivered medical care, food relief, scholarships, and financial empowerment to displaced families.
items.body:
On the 14th of September, Chiggy Nsofor Foundation (CNF) successfully carried out a significant outreach at the New Kuchingoro IDP camp in Abuja. Through the outreach tagged "Project HEEM: Humanitarian Aid, Education, Empowerment and Medical Care", CNF targeted the most pressing needs of camp residents and delivered essential food items, scholarships, empowerment and medical care to internally displaced individuals.

Camp residents and families from neighbouring communities benefited from free medical consultations, tests and medications, with services that included malaria and typhoid tests, blood pressure checks, diabetes screenings, HIV tests, among others. CNF also provided free medications to treat conditions including ulcer, fever, diarrhea, malnutrition and many more ailments. The medical team on-site, which included certified doctors, nurses, medical lab scientists and pharmacists, attended to men and women (both young and elderly), children, pregnant women, nursing mothers and their babies.

To address immediate hunger needs in the IDP camp, CNF distributed essential food supplies to several families. They were given non-perishable items like rice, beans, maize, garri, palm oil and more. Under the empowerment arm of the outreach, CNF financially empowered several small business owners to scale their businesses and provided them with logbooks for accountability purposes.

Children in the IDP camp were not left behind as we provided many students whose parents could not afford their fees with 3-year scholarships to continue their secondary school education as it aligns with our mission. They were also given educational materials such as school bags, books, and pens ensuring that they have access to learning opportunities and materials despite their challenging circumstances.

Speaking at the outreach, CNF's founder, Chiggy Nsofor said, "These people have been through so much, and we are here to bring them the support they need to live a healthier and better quality of life. Through Project HEEM, we aim to treat illnesses prevalent in IDP camps and empower them. Our commitment to the well-being of internally displaced persons remains unwavering."

The Assistant Camp Secretary, Mrs. Hannatu Katghaya, expressed profound appreciation on behalf of the community. She stated, "In this hardship, families cannot afford food, drugs or school fees, that is why I am amazed, excited, and happy. I really appreciate the Chiggy Nsofor Foundation for all they have done today."

Several beneficiaries also shared their heartfelt thanks for the timely assistance. As part of its ongoing mission, CNF plans to extend her outreach activities to other vulnerable communities across Nigeria, ensuring that those who are displaced continually receive the support they need.

items.title: Prioritising Maternal & Child Health: CNF Grants Medical Support to Patients in Kuje Hospitals
items.imageAlt: CNF team providing maternal and child health support at Kuje hospitals
items.excerpt: CNF's healthcare outreach at Kuje General Hospital and White Dove Hospital cleared medical bills for pregnant women, new mothers, and children in critical need.
items.body:
Chiggy Nsofor Foundation (CNF) recently launched a vital Healthcare Outreach targeting two hospitals in Kuje, Abuja: Kuje General Hospital and White Dove Hospital. This initiative aimed to provide essential support to pregnant women, new mothers and young children who are unable to afford their medical bills and medications, demonstrating our commitment to making healthcare a fundamental right for all.

During our visit we encountered several patients in critical need of assistance. Patients who benefitted from our intervention include new mothers who could not pay their neonatal and postnatal bills, children suffering from pneumonia and malnourishment whose parents could not afford their treatment and medications, and patients who were treating ulcers.

The Foundation cleared the medical bills for the pregnant women, new mothers and their newborns ensuring that their financial burdens were alleviated. Among these patients helped was a new mother whose baby was in dire need of oxygen but could not afford it. Our foundation was glad to offset the bills to enable her baby access to the oxygen needed.

A beneficiary of our healthcare outreach was a child diagnosed with chronic pneumonia. Her mother explained that she had been diagnosed with pneumonia and there was no money to treat her. CNF stepped in and paid for her daughter's treatment and also bought the prescribed drugs to aid her recovery.

Another heart-wrenching case was that of a severely malnourished child. Her father related the struggle he was facing and his inability to afford her medical bills and drugs due to economic hardship. The Foundation paid his child's medical expenses, bought all her prescribed medications and also provided funds for her feeding, ensuring the little child has a comprehensive path to full recovery.

In addition, CNF also offered assistance to ulcer patients who could not afford their medical bills by offsetting their bills. These interventions by CNF have had a profound impact, offering relief and hope to families grappling with health challenges in the midst of economic hardship.

Expressing gratitude to the Foundation, the Matron of Kuje General Hospital said, "Thank you for your Foundation coming to the hospital to see the patients, thank you for the bills that were offset. We pray that God will bless you people richly." The Matron of White Dove Hospital, Matron Adesola, also expressed deep appreciation on behalf of the hospital.

CNF's Healthcare outreach highlights the importance and impact of our intervention and support to pregnant women, new mothers, their newborns and children's health in general. By addressing their immediate medical needs, we are not only saving lives but also building a healthier community.

items.title: CNF's Academic Outreach Gives Hope and Uplifts Futures
items.imageAlt: CNF academic outreach team at St. Philips Academy, Mararaba
items.excerpt: CNF's May academic outreach at St. Philips Academy, Mararaba paid school fees, cleared outstanding debts, and covered WASSCE fees for students in need.
items.body:
The Chiggy Nsofor Foundation (CNF) embarked on an impactful outreach this May, dedicated to wiping tears and putting smiles on the faces of some students of St. Philips Academy, a missionary school in the Mararaba area of Abuja. The academic outreach was targeted at both male and female senior students who could not afford to pay their school fees by alleviating the financial burdens on their parents.

Beyond payment of the current term school fees for many, the foundation's efforts extended to offsetting outstanding debts of many more students of the same school by clearing a backlog of unpaid fees, thereby giving these students the opportunity to thrive and focus academically, unburdened by the continuous thoughts of debts. In addition, CNF paid the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) fees for students who had not yet made payments due to financial hardship.

The outreach was concluded with a health talk led by Health and Wellness Advocate, Lois Amele on the importance of menstrual hygiene for senior female students which equipped them with the knowledge and resources (distribution of sanitary pads and tissue papers by CNF) essential for their menstrual hygiene.

Speaking on the success of the outreach, CNF Founder, Chiggy Nsofor noted that, "What happened here today exceeded my expectations and I am really glad. The result was really beautiful. We were able to pay current term fees and backlog fees from previous terms for students who were owing." She encouraged them on the need to remain in school for a greater future.

Expressing gratitude to CNF Founder, Rev. Tony-Dada Aderomose, Founder of St. Philips Academy, said, "I am highly impressed at your coming to this school and with this work you have done. You are building them up, you are building a new Nigeria. If these children are built up, I'm sure that Nigeria will be good and in fact the whole world will be good."

Emmanuella Andy, one of the students whose fees were paid in full appreciated the foundation for their efforts. She stated, "I want to thank you very much for paying my school fees. It has not been easy for me and my parents. I'm very grateful. Thank you very much."

As the success of the May academic outreach is reflected upon, it serves as a reminder of the profound impact that collective action can achieve. Each student supported represents a beacon of hope for a more inclusive future. The Chiggy Nsofor Foundation's commitment to empowering individuals through education remains unwavering.

items.title: CNF Extends Support to Vulnerable Families in Mangu, Plateau State
items.imageAlt: CNF volunteers with food relief supplies during outreach in Mangu, Plateau State
items.excerpt: CNF conducted a food relief outreach in Mangu LGA, Plateau State, supporting families in Kantoma community affected by insecurity in Northern Nigeria.
items.body:
The Chiggy Nsofor Foundation (CNF) recently conducted a food relief outreach targeted at families affected by insecurities in Northern Nigeria. This initiative highlights the Foundation's ongoing effort to eradicate poverty in the country by supporting disadvantaged communities with vital food items.

The outreach, which was held in Mangu Local Government Area (LGA) of Plateau state on April 13, benefited several families from Kantoma community. Beneficiaries of the programme were given food items such as rice, beans, corn, garri, oil, snacks for children, and many more.

Additionally, the volunteers and representatives of CNF spoke with beneficiaries, discussing their needs and how insecurity in the area has impacted their lives and livelihood. Plateau, the twelfth largest Nigerian state, has witnessed increasing insecurity, including attacks by gunmen and banditry. This affirms the critical need for initiatives like the Chiggy Nsofor Foundation's food relief efforts.

Speaking during the presentation, the Founder, Chiggy Nsofor reiterated the mission and commitment of the foundation to fighting poverty, emphasizing ongoing efforts to provide relief to those in need. She also expressed sincere appreciation to beneficiaries and their families.

In February, many vulnerable families benefited from CNF food relief outreach. These families from Changal, Kikau, Gaude, Kinat, Tul kinat, Jwak and Maitumbi communities all assembled in Tuwan community of Plateau state and were given essential food items.

The Foundation has supported a large number of families in Plateau state since its launch three months prior, demonstrating tangible impact through vital food assistance.

items.title: CNF Kicks Off Its Inaugural Outreach with Food Relief Programme in Plateau
items.imageAlt: CNF inaugural food relief outreach with community members in Tuwan, Plateau State
items.excerpt: CNF's inaugural food relief outreach in Plateau State distributed essential supplies to families across underserved communities, a milestone that launched the foundation's mission.
items.body:
In a heartfelt gesture of compassion and support, the Chiggy Nsofor Foundation successfully conducted an inaugural outreach program in Plateau State reaching several families in need. The Food Relief initiative aimed to supply essential food items to families in underserved communities in the region.

This initiative, carried out in collaboration with dedicated volunteers, distributed vital supplies including rice, garri, salt, beans, corn, cooking oil and children's snacks to families both facing economic hardships and insecurity. These items were joyously received by the beneficiaries. Beneficiaries trooped into Tuwan in Plateau state from Changal, Kikau, Gaude, Kinat, Tul kinat, Jwak and Maitumbi communities.

Plateau State, known for its diverse cultures, has also experienced its share of socio-economic challenges. The Chiggy Nsofor Foundation's intervention highlights its commitment to addressing some of these issues and improving the quality of life for the vulnerable in the state.

Speaking on behalf of the organization, Chiggy Nsofor expressed gratitude for the opportunity to serve the community. "We are honoured to have the chance to make a positive impact in Plateau State," said Nsofor. "Our foundation is committed to supporting families facing hardships, and we hope to continue expanding our outreach efforts in the future."

The beneficiaries, who welcomed the assistance with smiles and heartfelt appreciation, emphasized the importance of such initiatives in bridging gaps during challenging times. "This support means a lot to us," remarked one recipient. "It's a blessing to know that there are organizations like the Chiggy Nsofor Foundation looking out for us."

This outreach in Plateau State marks the beginning of the foundation's future initiatives aimed at making a tangible difference in the lives of those in need. As the organization continues to grow and expand its reach, it remains committed to its mission of improving the quality of life of many.
